user.title: Set up HEMS
user.description:
HEMS automatically distributes your PV surplus to hot water, home battery and flexible loads.

**How it works:** the meter at the grid connection reports whether you are currently exporting (surplus) or importing power. Combined with the PV forecast, battery state and your priorities, this drives the recommendation and, later, the control.

The setup then guides you step by step through your devices: PV forecasts, storage, hot water, plus switchable and modulated loads. Every step can be skipped and every entry can be edited at any time later via **Configure**.

data_description.meter_entity: Sensor with the current power at the grid connection point in watts. Expected: positive = import, negative = export.
data_description.invert_meter: Enable if your meter reports export as a positive value.
data_description.pv_power_entity: Sensor with the current total PV production across all planes. Used for the load flow and to refine the recommendation.
data_description.invert_pv_power: Enable if your inverter reports PV power with a flipped sign (negative = production).
data_description.pv_minus_battery: Enable if PV and battery are measured at the same point (hybrid inverter), so the PV reading contains the battery power. HEMS then subtracts the battery power from the measured PV (discharge lowers it, charge raises it).
data_description.weather_entity: Weather entity whose daily forecast feeds the planning: on an overcast next day HEMS fully charges the battery instead of covering only the night.
data_description.baseline_load_w: Typical continuous consumption of the house during the day without large consumers (fridge, network, standby).
data_description.night_load_w: Initial value for night-time consumption. HEMS learns the real value automatically from meter statistics after a few days.
data_description.priority_mode: Where should surplus go first? "Automatic" fills the battery first when yield is scarce so the night is covered; with plenty of yield the EV may charge first. Hot-water base heating always has top priority.
data_description.free_capacity_kwh: The "Capacity free" binary sensor turns on when this much energy is available over the given duration without touching the reserve or the night coverage.
data_description.free_capacity_h: Duration over which the energy demand must be covered. PV surplus expected within this window counts towards the free capacity.

add_forecast.title: PV forecast plane
add_forecast.description: A **PV forecast plane** provides the expected solar production, e.g. from the Forecast.Solar or Solcast integration. Add multiple planes (east/west roof) separately — HEMS sums them automatically.

data_description.name: A short label for this forecast plane, e.g. the roof orientation (used only for display).
data_description.energy_today: Sensor with the forecast total PV energy for today (kWh), from your forecast integration (e.g. Forecast.Solar, Solcast).
data_description.energy_remaining: Sensor with the forecast remaining PV energy for the rest of today (kWh). Feeds the live surplus and recommendation calculations.
data_description.energy_tomorrow: Sensor with the forecast total PV energy for tomorrow (kWh). Used to decide whether the battery should be charged fully today as a buffer against a poor day ahead.

add_storage.title: Storage
add_storage.description: A **storage** (home battery) buffers PV surplus for the night. HEMS derives a target state of charge from night consumption and reserve and schedules charging within the solar window.

data.name: Name
data.soc_set_entity: Target SoC entity (soc_set, device-side charge cap, optional)

data_description.charge_setpoint_entity: Number entity HEMS can use to set the current charging power.
data_description.discharge_setpoint_entity: Number entity HEMS can use to set the current discharge power (e.g. “discharge at 500 W now”).
data_description.reserve_soc: The battery should not be discharged below this level (emergency reserve).
data_description.max_charge_w: Charging power limit; determines how quickly the battery fills within the solar window.
data_description.max_discharge_w: Limit of the discharge power; the battery cannot deliver more than this to the house.
data_description.cold_reserve: This storage joins discharging only when the average SoC of the other storages drops below the reserve threshold (with hysteresis). It always participates in charging, proportionally to its free capacity.
data_description.name: A short label for this storage, e.g. its physical location or unit name.
data_description.soc_entity: Sensor with the current state of charge in percent.
data_description.power_entity: Sensor with the current charge/discharge power in watts. Convention: positive = discharging into the house, negative = charging. Used for the load-flow display and the auto-mode control loop.
data_description.mode_entity: Optional select/input_select HEMS toggles between charging and discharging direction (e.g. Zendure's ac_mode). Only needed if your storage requires a mode switch in addition to a setpoint.
data_description.mode_charge_option: The option value that puts the storage into charging mode. Must match one of the select's available options exactly (case-sensitive) — the config check flags it otherwise.
data_description.mode_discharge_option: The option value that puts the storage into discharging mode. Must match one of the select's available options exactly (case-sensitive) — the config check flags it otherwise.
data_description.soc_set_entity: Optional number entity that caps how far the storage charges on its own (device-side target SoC). Some storages ignore an input power limit of 0 and keep charging toward this target regardless — set it if that applies to yours.
data_description.capacity_kwh: Usable capacity of this storage; used to distribute charge/discharge power across multiple storages and for the SoC forecast.

add_thermal.title: Hot water storage
add_thermal.description: A **hot water storage** stores surplus as heat. The base target is always maintained — from the grid if necessary. Heating up to the comfort target happens only on PV surplus.

data.name: Name
data.boost_soc_on: PV boost: battery SoC to start (%)
data.boost_soc_off: PV boost: battery SoC to stop (%)
data.boost_saldo_on_w: PV boost: grid balance to start (W)
data.boost_saldo_off_w: PV boost: grid balance to stop (W)
data.control_entity: Control entity for auto mode (water_heater, or a switch)

data_description.base_target: This temperature is always maintained, from the grid if necessary.
data_description.comfort_target: Heating up to this temperature only happens on PV surplus.
data_description.block_start: Start of the daily period in which no hot water is prepared. Leave both empty for no blocking.
data_description.block_end: End of the blocked period. An end before the start means the window runs over midnight (e.g. 18:00 to 06:00).
data_description.legionella_weekday: Weekly hygiene window: on this day the target is raised to the legionella target regardless of surplus — from the grid if necessary. "Disabled" turns the feature off.
data_description.legionella_start: Local start time of the weekly legionella window.
data_description.legionella_end: End of the window. An end before the start runs over midnight.
data_description.legionella_target: Target temperature held during the legionella window.
data_description.boost_soc_on: Heating to the comfort target is only recommended once the total storage SoC reaches this level.
data_description.boost_soc_off: The boost recommendation ends when the SoC falls below this level (hysteresis).
data_description.boost_saldo_on_w: Grid balance that must be reached to start the boost; negative = export (e.g. -2800 = exporting 2.8 kW).
data_description.boost_saldo_off_w: Grid balance at which the boost ends (positive = import).
data_description.name: A short label for this hot-water system (used only for display).
data_description.temp_entity: Sensor with the current hot-water temperature. Without it, HEMS still recommends a target but cannot show or verify the actual temperature.
data_description.control_entity: Entity HEMS switches on/off in auto mode. A water_heater also carries the target temperature; a switch only turns it on/off — then set the target on the number below.
data_description.setpoint_entity: Number HEMS writes the target temperature to when the control entity is a switch (e.g. a Modbus heat pump exposing an enable switch and a target-temperature number separately). Leave empty for a water_heater.

add_switchable.title: Switchable load
add_switchable.description: **Switchable (sheddable) loads** are devices HEMS can only turn on or off — their power cannot be modulated. Examples: heat pump (SG-Ready/blocking contact), heating rod, pool pump. Minimum runtime and minimum pause protect the device from frequent cycling.

data_description.min_on_min: Once switched on, the device stays on for at least this long.
data_description.min_off_min: After switching off, the device stays off for at least this long.
data_description.max_block_min: The device is never blocked for longer than this per day.
data_description.priority: 1 = highest priority. When surplus is scarce, loads with higher priority are served first.
data_description.heat_coupled: Only for loads whose consumption follows the outdoor temperature (heat pump, heating rod). Only those feed the heating-degree-hour model used for demand forecasting. Surplus-driven loads such as a pool pump or dehumidifier stay off.
data_description.name: A short label for this load (used only for display, e.g. in the recommendation and load-flow card).
data_description.switch_entity: Switch (or climate) entity HEMS turns on and off based on surplus.
data_description.power_entity: Sensor with the current power draw in watts. HEMS learns the expected power from it while the load is running, used to decide whether surplus covers it.

add_modulated.title: Modulated load
add_modulated.description: **Modulated loads** can adjust their power consumption continuously. The typical example is a wallbox whose charging current (in amperes) can be regulated between a minimum and maximum. HEMS continuously tracks the setpoint to the available surplus.

data_description.current_entity: Number entity used to set the current setpoint.
data_description.switch_entity: Optional switch HEMS can use to turn the device on and off entirely (e.g. wallbox charging enable).
data_description.min_on_min: Once started, the device runs for at least this long before HEMS stops it (e.g. charge the EV for at least 10 minutes).
data_description.min_a: The device cannot operate below this current (wallbox minimum is usually 6 A).
data_description.priority: 1 = highest priority. When surplus is scarce, loads with higher priority are served first.
data_description.name: A short label for this load (used only for display, e.g. the wallbox name).
data_description.power_entity: Sensor with the current power draw in watts. Used for the load-flow display and to learn the load's actual demand.
data_description.max_a: The device is never commanded above this current.
data_description.phases: Number of connected phases; used to convert between current (A) and power (W).
data_description.min_off_min: After HEMS stops the device, it stays off for at least this long before it can restart.

heating_menu.title: Heating circuit (step 5 of 7)
heating_menu.description:
A **heating circuit** (e.g. heat pump) gets a mode recommendation (heat/cool/off) from outdoor-temperature thresholds with hysteresis, plus a weather-compensated flow temperature from the heating curve. Room heat demand raises the curve; without demand the flow drops to the minimum (setback). During the summer lock months heating is never recommended.

data.name: Name
data.control_entity: Control entity for auto mode (climate, or a mode select)
data.setpoint_entity: Flow-temperature number (only with a mode select)
data.mode_heat_option: Mode-select option for heating (only with a mode select)
data.mode_off_option: Mode-select option for off (only with a mode select)
data.antitakt_starts: Anti-cycling: compressor starts per window (0 = off)
data.curve_from_analysis: Adopt heating curve from the heat pump analysis

data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Temperature sensor that drives the mode decision and the heating curve.
data_description.demand_entity: Sensor with the room heat demand in percent (e.g. PID thermostat output, several rooms combined via a template sensor). Raises the flow target by up to 5 K; below 1 % demand the flow drops to the minimum (setback).
data_description.heat_on_c: Heating is recommended once the outdoor temperature falls to this value.
data_description.heat_off_c: Heating ends once the outdoor temperature rises to this value (hysteresis).
data_description.cool_on_c: Cooling is recommended once the outdoor temperature rises to this value.
data_description.cool_off_c: Cooling ends once the outdoor temperature falls to this value (hysteresis).
data_description.frost_on_c: Frost protection forces heating once the outdoor temperature falls to this value — even during the summer lock.
data_description.frost_off_c: Frost protection ends once the outdoor temperature rises to this value (hysteresis to prevent cycling).
data_description.heat_lock_from_month: During the lock months (inclusive) heating is only forced by frost protection, otherwise never recommended (summer lock).
data_description.heat_lock_to_month: Last month (inclusive) of the summer lock. A start after the end wraps around new year.
data_description.curve_base_c: Flow temperature target at 0 °C outdoor temperature.
data_description.curve_slope: Reduction of the flow target per degree of outdoor temperature.
data_description.vlt_min_c: The flow target never falls below this value while heating.
data_description.vlt_min_cold_c: Minimum flow target when it is colder than 5 °C outside.
data_description.vlt_max_c: The flow target never exceeds this value.
data_description.name: A short label for this heating circuit (used only for display).
data_description.control_entity: Entity HEMS sets the mode on in auto mode. A climate carries mode and flow target itself; a select (e.g. a Modbus operating-mode register) needs the flow number and mode-option fields below. Without a control entity, the recommendation is only shown, not applied.
data_description.setpoint_entity: Number HEMS writes the flow-temperature target to when the control entity is a mode select (e.g. a Modbus heat pump with a separate operating-mode select and flow-target number). Leave empty for a climate.
data_description.mode_heat_option: The select option that means heating (e.g. "Heizen"), written when HEMS recommends heating. Only with a select control.
data_description.mode_cool_option: The select option that means cooling (e.g. "Kühlen"). Leave empty for heat-only devices.
data_description.mode_off_option: The select option that means off / hot-water-only (e.g. "Aus/nur Warmwasser"), written when HEMS recommends off. Only with a select control.
data_description.silent_switch_entity: Optional switch/input_boolean HEMS turns on during low-surplus periods to run the heat pump in its quiet mode.
data_description.season_select_entity: Optional input_select/select HEMS uses to switch a heat pump between heating and cooling direction, if your device needs an explicit season switch.
data_description.fault_entity: Optional binary_sensor (on = fault) or sensor (value ≠ 0/“ok” = error code) HEMS watches to detect heat-pump faults and warn you via push notification / repair issue. Informational only — it controls nothing.
data_description.dhw_active_entity: Optional binary_sensor/switch/input_boolean that is on while the heat pump is charging the hot-water tank. While it is on, HEMS leaves the heating circuit untouched: many heat pumps raise the flow setpoint themselves during a charge and write back over whatever HEMS sets, so both keep overwriting each other every cycle. Leave empty if your device has no such feedback; behaviour is then unchanged.
data_description.compressor_entity: Optional binary_sensor/switch/input_boolean that is on while the compressor runs. HEMS counts its starts and, in cooling mode, forces a pause once there are too many of them - short cycles wear the compressor out, and most units offer no setting for it. Leave empty if your device has no such feedback; anti-cycling then stays off.
data_description.room_temp_entity: Optional temperature sensor of a representative room. Together with room humidity, HEMS derives the dew point from it and keeps the cooling flow above it - otherwise water condenses on floors or walls with surface cooling. Only both fields together take effect; leave one empty and the cooling setpoint applies unchanged.
data_description.room_humidity_entity: Optional humidity sensor of the same room, in % relative humidity. Only together with room temperature does it yield a dew point. Without this role the lower limit for the cooling flow stays off, and the flow runs to the configured cooling setpoint even if that is below the dew point.
data_description.dewpoint_margin_k: How far above the dew point the cooling flow should stay. Flow temperature is not surface temperature - screed and plaster sit in between, and the surface stays warmer than the water. 2 K is a reasonable start; 0 puts the limit exactly on the dew point.
data_description.antitakt_starts: Number of compressor starts within the observation window that triggers a forced pause. 0 switches anti-cycling off. Applies to heating and cooling alike, but never during frost protection.
data_description.antitakt_window_min: Length of the window the starts are counted in. The window rolls along: what counts is every start younger than that span.
data_description.antitakt_pause_min: How long HEMS recommends 'off' after too many starts. This limits the START RATE, not the length of a single cycle: the four-minute gap the unit allows itself becomes a long one.
data_description.curve_from_analysis: Instead of the base point and slope above, HEMS uses the measured recommendation from the heat pump analysis role. Adopted at most once a day, only on a reliable data basis and only for a noticeable difference — the recommendation comes from operation HEMS produced with the previous one, and without damping the curve would drift. The values above stay and apply again as soon as the switch is off.

add_analysis.title: Heat pump analysis
add_analysis.description:
The **heat pump analysis** measures how well the unit actually performs: COP against the data sheet, spread, cycling, the building's heat loss and a heating curve suggestion.

It only advises and never switches — setpoints go through the heating circuit role. Five measurement inputs are required, two more improve the result.

data.name: Name
data.durchfluss_nominal_lh: Nominal flow rate without a meter (l/h)

data_description.name: A short label for this heat pump (display only).
data_description.preset: Model-specific, not brand-specific: the Therma V range alone has four clearly different curves. If your model is missing, a generic type works — the data basis is downgraded accordingly.
data_description.vorlauf_temp: Measured flow temperature, not reconstructed from the return.
data_description.durchfluss: Heating water flow rate. Without it the analysis uses the nominal flow from the device curve, reports “flow rate estimated” and never marks the COP as reliable. The unit is read from the entity and never guessed: l/min instead of l/h skews every COP by a factor of 60.
data_description.leistung_elektrisch: Ideally the heat pump only, without other loads on the same meter.
data_description.aussentemperatur: An independent sensor beats the built-in one: that often sits in a sunlit enclosure and reads far too high when the unit is idle.
data_description.verdichter_frequenz: Without it, cycling is estimated from the electrical power.
data_description.betriebsart: Separates heating, hot water and defrost. Without it, heating and hot water blend into one figure — allowed, but it downgrades the data basis.
data_description.standby_w: Power drawn without the compressor running (circulation pump, electronics). 0 means: take the value from the device curve.
data_description.durchfluss_nominal_lh: Only needed if no flow sensor is set above. Without either, the analysis discards every reading: no flow means no thermal output and therefore no COP. The four LG profiles carry the value, the six generic ones do not — it depends on the circulation pump and the hydraulics, not on the device model. Read it off the pump (m³/h × 1000) or compute it from a known operating point: thermal output [W] ÷ (spread [K] × 1.163). 0 means: take the value from the device curve.
data_description.warmwasser_aktiv: Feedback that the unit is currently charging the tank — a binary_sensor, switch or input_boolean. Separate from the operating mode because many units track both independently: the heating circuit says cooling while a hot water charge runs in parallel with priority. While it is on, the analysis counts the operation as hot water, whatever the mode entity reports. Without it, every tank charge in winter would count as heating — high flow temperature, wide spread — skewing the very figure the operating mode is meant to protect.

edit_device.title: Edit device
edit_device.description: Select the entry you want to change. All values can be adjusted afterwards.

data_description.name: A short label for this forecast plane, e.g. the roof orientation (used only for display).
data_description.energy_today: Sensor with the forecast total PV energy for today (kWh), from your forecast integration (e.g. Forecast.Solar, Solcast).
data_description.energy_remaining: Sensor with the forecast remaining PV energy for the rest of today (kWh). Feeds the live surplus and recommendation calculations.
data_description.energy_tomorrow: Sensor with the forecast total PV energy for tomorrow (kWh). Used to decide whether the battery should be charged fully today as a buffer against a poor day ahead.

data.name: Name
data.soc_set_entity: Target SoC entity (soc_set, device-side charge cap, optional)

data_description.charge_setpoint_entity: Number entity HEMS can use to set the current charging power.
data_description.discharge_setpoint_entity: Number entity HEMS can use to set the current discharge power (e.g. “discharge at 500 W now”).
data_description.reserve_soc: The battery should not be discharged below this level (emergency reserve).
data_description.max_charge_w: Charging power limit; determines how quickly the battery fills within the solar window.
data_description.max_discharge_w: Limit of the discharge power; the battery cannot deliver more than this to the house.
data_description.cold_reserve: This storage joins discharging only when the average SoC of the other storages drops below the reserve threshold (with hysteresis). It always participates in charging, proportionally to its free capacity.
data_description.name: A short label for this storage, e.g. its physical location or unit name.
data_description.soc_entity: Sensor with the current state of charge in percent.
data_description.power_entity: Sensor with the current charge/discharge power in watts. Convention: positive = discharging into the house, negative = charging. Used for the load-flow display and the auto-mode control loop.
data_description.mode_entity: Optional select/input_select HEMS toggles between charging and discharging direction (e.g. Zendure's ac_mode). Only needed if your storage requires a mode switch in addition to a setpoint.
data_description.mode_charge_option: The option value that puts the storage into charging mode. Must match one of the select's available options exactly (case-sensitive) — the config check flags it otherwise.
data_description.mode_discharge_option: The option value that puts the storage into discharging mode. Must match one of the select's available options exactly (case-sensitive) — the config check flags it otherwise.
data_description.soc_set_entity: Optional number entity that caps how far the storage charges on its own (device-side target SoC). Some storages ignore an input power limit of 0 and keep charging toward this target regardless — set it if that applies to yours.
data_description.capacity_kwh: Usable capacity of this storage; used to distribute charge/discharge power across multiple storages and for the SoC forecast.

data.name: Name
data.boost_soc_on: PV boost: battery SoC to start (%)
data.boost_soc_off: PV boost: battery SoC to stop (%)
data.boost_saldo_on_w: PV boost: grid balance to start (W)
data.boost_saldo_off_w: PV boost: grid balance to stop (W)
data.control_entity: Control entity for auto mode (water_heater, or a switch)

data_description.base_target: This temperature is always maintained, from the grid if necessary.
data_description.comfort_target: Heating up to this temperature only happens on PV surplus.
data_description.block_start: Start of the daily period in which no hot water is prepared. Leave both empty for no blocking.
data_description.block_end: End of the blocked period. An end before the start means the window runs over midnight (e.g. 18:00 to 06:00).
data_description.legionella_weekday: Weekly hygiene window: on this day the target is raised to the legionella target regardless of surplus — from the grid if necessary. "Disabled" turns the feature off.
data_description.legionella_start: Local start time of the weekly legionella window.
data_description.legionella_end: End of the window. An end before the start runs over midnight.
data_description.legionella_target: Target temperature held during the legionella window.
data_description.boost_soc_on: Heating to the comfort target is only recommended once the total storage SoC reaches this level.
data_description.boost_soc_off: The boost recommendation ends when the SoC falls below this level (hysteresis).
data_description.boost_saldo_on_w: Grid balance that must be reached to start the boost; negative = export (e.g. -2800 = exporting 2.8 kW).
data_description.boost_saldo_off_w: Grid balance at which the boost ends (positive = import).
data_description.name: A short label for this hot-water system (used only for display).
data_description.temp_entity: Sensor with the current hot-water temperature. Without it, HEMS still recommends a target but cannot show or verify the actual temperature.
data_description.control_entity: Entity HEMS switches on/off in auto mode. A water_heater also carries the target temperature; a switch only turns it on/off — then set the target on the number below.
data_description.setpoint_entity: Number HEMS writes the target temperature to when the control entity is a switch (e.g. a Modbus heat pump exposing an enable switch and a target-temperature number separately). Leave empty for a water_heater.

edit_switchable.title: Edit switchable load
edit_switchable.description: Adjust settings for "{name}". Switchable loads only know on/off; the timings protect the device from frequent cycling.

data_description.min_on_min: Once switched on, the device stays on for at least this long.
data_description.min_off_min: After switching off, the device stays off for at least this long.
data_description.max_block_min: The device is never blocked for longer than this per day.
data_description.priority: 1 = highest priority. When surplus is scarce, loads with higher priority are served first.
data_description.heat_coupled: Only for loads whose consumption follows the outdoor temperature (heat pump, heating rod). Only those feed the heating-degree-hour model used for demand forecasting. Surplus-driven loads such as a pool pump or dehumidifier stay off.
data_description.name: A short label for this load (used only for display, e.g. in the recommendation and load-flow card).
data_description.switch_entity: Switch (or climate) entity HEMS turns on and off based on surplus.
data_description.power_entity: Sensor with the current power draw in watts. HEMS learns the expected power from it while the load is running, used to decide whether surplus covers it.

edit_modulated.title: Edit modulated load
edit_modulated.description: Adjust settings for "{name}". Modulated loads regulate their power continuously via the current setpoint.

data_description.current_entity: Number entity used to set the current setpoint.
data_description.switch_entity: Optional switch HEMS can use to turn the device on and off entirely (e.g. wallbox charging enable).
data_description.min_on_min: Once started, the device runs for at least this long before HEMS stops it (e.g. charge the EV for at least 10 minutes).
data_description.min_a: The device cannot operate below this current (wallbox minimum is usually 6 A).
data_description.priority: 1 = highest priority. When surplus is scarce, loads with higher priority are served first.
data_description.name: A short label for this load (used only for display, e.g. the wallbox name).
data_description.power_entity: Sensor with the current power draw in watts. Used for the load-flow display and to learn the load's actual demand.
data_description.max_a: The device is never commanded above this current.
data_description.phases: Number of connected phases; used to convert between current (A) and power (W).
data_description.min_off_min: After HEMS stops the device, it stays off for at least this long before it can restart.

remove_device.title: Remove device
remove_device.description: The selected entry is removed from the configuration. The real device is not affected.

data_description.device: Pick the device to remove. This does not delete the underlying entities, only HEMS's configuration for it.

general.title: Base values & priorities
general.description: These values were set during onboarding and can be changed here at any time.

data_description.meter_entity: Sensor with the current power at the grid connection point in watts. Expected: positive = import, negative = export.
data_description.invert_meter: Enable if your meter reports export as a positive value.
data_description.pv_power_entity: Sensor with the current total PV production across all planes. Used for the load flow and to refine the recommendation.
data_description.invert_pv_power: Enable if your inverter reports PV power with a flipped sign (negative = production).
data_description.pv_minus_battery: Enable if PV and battery are measured at the same point (hybrid inverter), so the PV reading contains the battery power. HEMS then subtracts the battery power from the measured PV (discharge lowers it, charge raises it).
data_description.weather_entity: Weather entity whose daily forecast feeds the planning: on an overcast next day HEMS fully charges the battery instead of covering only the night.
data_description.baseline_load_w: Typical continuous consumption of the house during the day without large consumers.
data_description.night_load_w: Fallback for night-time consumption until HEMS has learned it from statistics.
data_description.priority_mode: Where should surplus go first? "Automatic" fills the battery first when yield is scarce so the night is covered; with plenty of yield the EV may charge first. Hot-water base heating always has top priority.
data_description.free_capacity_kwh: The "Capacity free" binary sensor turns on when this much energy is available over the given duration without touching the reserve or the night coverage.
data_description.free_capacity_h: Duration over which the energy demand must be covered. PV surplus expected within this window counts towards the free capacity.

add_heating.title: Heating circuit
add_heating.description: A **heating circuit** (e.g. heat pump) gets a mode recommendation (heat/cool/off) from outdoor-temperature thresholds with hysteresis, plus a weather-compensated flow temperature from the heating curve. Room heat demand raises the curve; without demand the flow drops to the minimum (setback). During the summer lock months heating is never recommended.

data.name: Name
data.control_entity: Control entity for auto mode (climate, or a mode select)
data.setpoint_entity: Flow-temperature number (only with a mode select)
data.mode_heat_option: Mode-select option for heating (only with a mode select)
data.mode_off_option: Mode-select option for off (only with a mode select)
data.antitakt_starts: Anti-cycling: compressor starts per window (0 = off)
data.curve_from_analysis: Adopt heating curve from the heat pump analysis

data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Temperature sensor that drives the mode decision and the heating curve.
data_description.demand_entity: Sensor with the room heat demand in percent (e.g. PID thermostat output, several rooms combined via a template sensor). Raises the flow target by up to 5 K; below 1 % demand the flow drops to the minimum (setback).
data_description.heat_on_c: Heating is recommended once the outdoor temperature falls to this value.
data_description.heat_off_c: Heating ends once the outdoor temperature rises to this value (hysteresis).
data_description.cool_on_c: Cooling is recommended once the outdoor temperature rises to this value.
data_description.cool_off_c: Cooling ends once the outdoor temperature falls to this value (hysteresis).
data_description.frost_on_c: Frost protection forces heating once the outdoor temperature falls to this value — even during the summer lock.
data_description.frost_off_c: Frost protection ends once the outdoor temperature rises to this value (hysteresis to prevent cycling).
data_description.heat_lock_from_month: During the lock months (inclusive) heating is only forced by frost protection, otherwise never recommended (summer lock).
data_description.heat_lock_to_month: Last month (inclusive) of the summer lock. A start after the end wraps around new year.
data_description.curve_base_c: Flow temperature target at 0 °C outdoor temperature.
data_description.curve_slope: Reduction of the flow target per degree of outdoor temperature.
data_description.vlt_min_c: The flow target never falls below this value while heating.
data_description.vlt_min_cold_c: Minimum flow target when it is colder than 5 °C outside.
data_description.vlt_max_c: The flow target never exceeds this value.
data_description.name: A short label for this heating circuit (used only for display).
data_description.control_entity: Entity HEMS sets the mode on in auto mode. A climate carries mode and flow target itself; a select (e.g. a Modbus operating-mode register) needs the flow number and mode-option fields below. Without a control entity, the recommendation is only shown, not applied.
data_description.setpoint_entity: Number HEMS writes the flow-temperature target to when the control entity is a mode select (e.g. a Modbus heat pump with a separate operating-mode select and flow-target number). Leave empty for a climate.
data_description.mode_heat_option: The select option that means heating (e.g. "Heizen"), written when HEMS recommends heating. Only with a select control.
data_description.mode_cool_option: The select option that means cooling (e.g. "Kühlen"). Leave empty for heat-only devices.
data_description.mode_off_option: The select option that means off / hot-water-only (e.g. "Aus/nur Warmwasser"), written when HEMS recommends off. Only with a select control.
data_description.silent_switch_entity: Optional switch/input_boolean HEMS turns on during low-surplus periods to run the heat pump in its quiet mode.
data_description.season_select_entity: Optional input_select/select HEMS uses to switch a heat pump between heating and cooling direction, if your device needs an explicit season switch.
data_description.fault_entity: Optional binary_sensor (on = fault) or sensor (value ≠ 0/“ok” = error code) HEMS watches to detect heat-pump faults and warn you via push notification / repair issue. Informational only — it controls nothing.
data_description.dhw_active_entity: Optional binary_sensor/switch/input_boolean that is on while the heat pump is charging the hot-water tank. While it is on, HEMS leaves the heating circuit untouched: many heat pumps raise the flow setpoint themselves during a charge and write back over whatever HEMS sets, so both keep overwriting each other every cycle. Leave empty if your device has no such feedback; behaviour is then unchanged.
data_description.compressor_entity: Optional binary_sensor/switch/input_boolean that is on while the compressor runs. HEMS counts its starts and, in cooling mode, forces a pause once there are too many of them - short cycles wear the compressor out, and most units offer no setting for it. Leave empty if your device has no such feedback; anti-cycling then stays off.
data_description.room_temp_entity: Optional temperature sensor of a representative room. Together with room humidity, HEMS derives the dew point from it and keeps the cooling flow above it - otherwise water condenses on floors or walls with surface cooling. Only both fields together take effect; leave one empty and the cooling setpoint applies unchanged.
data_description.room_humidity_entity: Optional humidity sensor of the same room, in % relative humidity. Only together with room temperature does it yield a dew point. Without this role the lower limit for the cooling flow stays off, and the flow runs to the configured cooling setpoint even if that is below the dew point.
data_description.dewpoint_margin_k: How far above the dew point the cooling flow should stay. Flow temperature is not surface temperature - screed and plaster sit in between, and the surface stays warmer than the water. 2 K is a reasonable start; 0 puts the limit exactly on the dew point.
data_description.antitakt_starts: Number of compressor starts within the observation window that triggers a forced pause. 0 switches anti-cycling off. Applies to heating and cooling alike, but never during frost protection.
data_description.antitakt_window_min: Length of the window the starts are counted in. The window rolls along: what counts is every start younger than that span.
data_description.antitakt_pause_min: How long HEMS recommends 'off' after too many starts. This limits the START RATE, not the length of a single cycle: the four-minute gap the unit allows itself becomes a long one.
data_description.curve_from_analysis: Instead of the base point and slope above, HEMS uses the measured recommendation from the heat pump analysis role. Adopted at most once a day, only on a reliable data basis and only for a noticeable difference — the recommendation comes from operation HEMS produced with the previous one, and without damping the curve would drift. The values above stay and apply again as soon as the switch is off.

add_analysis.title: Heat pump analysis
add_analysis.description:
The **heat pump analysis** measures how well the unit actually performs: COP against the data sheet, spread, cycling, the building's heat loss and a heating curve suggestion.

It only advises and never switches — setpoints go through the heating circuit role. Five measurement inputs are required, two more improve the result.

data.name: Name
data.durchfluss_nominal_lh: Nominal flow rate without a meter (l/h)

data_description.name: A short label for this heat pump (display only).
data_description.preset: Model-specific, not brand-specific: the Therma V range alone has four clearly different curves. If your model is missing, a generic type works — the data basis is downgraded accordingly.
data_description.vorlauf_temp: Measured flow temperature, not reconstructed from the return.
data_description.durchfluss: Heating water flow rate. Without it the analysis uses the nominal flow from the device curve, reports “flow rate estimated” and never marks the COP as reliable. The unit is read from the entity and never guessed: l/min instead of l/h skews every COP by a factor of 60.
data_description.leistung_elektrisch: Ideally the heat pump only, without other loads on the same meter.
data_description.aussentemperatur: An independent sensor beats the built-in one: that often sits in a sunlit enclosure and reads far too high when the unit is idle.
data_description.verdichter_frequenz: Without it, cycling is estimated from the electrical power.
data_description.betriebsart: Separates heating, hot water and defrost. Without it, heating and hot water blend into one figure — allowed, but it downgrades the data basis.
data_description.standby_w: Power drawn without the compressor running (circulation pump, electronics). 0 means: take the value from the device curve.
data_description.durchfluss_nominal_lh: Only needed if no flow sensor is set above. Without either, the analysis discards every reading: no flow means no thermal output and therefore no COP. The four LG profiles carry the value, the six generic ones do not — it depends on the circulation pump and the hydraulics, not on the device model. Read it off the pump (m³/h × 1000) or compute it from a known operating point: thermal output [W] ÷ (spread [K] × 1.163). 0 means: take the value from the device curve.
data_description.warmwasser_aktiv: Feedback that the unit is currently charging the tank — a binary_sensor, switch or input_boolean. Separate from the operating mode because many units track both independently: the heating circuit says cooling while a hot water charge runs in parallel with priority. While it is on, the analysis counts the operation as hot water, whatever the mode entity reports. Without it, every tank charge in winter would count as heating — high flow temperature, wide spread — skewing the very figure the operating mode is meant to protect.

wp_stoerung.title: Heat pump {name}: fault reported
wp_stoerung.description: The heat pump “{name}” reports a fault (code/status: {code}) via {entity}. Please check the unit.

stoerung_quelle_weg.title: Heat pump {name}: fault signal unavailable
stoerung_quelle_weg.description: The fault entity “{entity}” of heat pump “{name}” is unavailable — a real fault would go unnoticed right now. Please check the connection.

config_fehler.title: HEMS: configuration error ({anzahl})
config_fehler.description:
Auto mode would fail with the current configuration:
{fehler}
